reason: Conversation 1 asked the ideal first question (what lights/sounds, does the door click shut), told the customer to unplug before inspecting the catch, reached the correct broken-striker diagnosis, and added a sensible hinge/alignment check while the model number was sought; it never suggested bypassing the switch. Conversation 2 reached the same correct diagnosis only because the customer volunteered the snapped tongue, after a scattershot opener about cool-air programmes and filter cleaning, and then repeated the identical heading, panel and text across three turns while oddly implying the door 'won't open'. Both ended without resolving the unreadable model sticker (neither suggested a torch, photo or rear rating plate) and neither explicitly warned against taping the switch, so the gap is modest, but Conversation 1 was more targeted, safer and less repetitive.
